high_level_overview.overview: This JCL job, named **WAITSTEP**, is designed to introduce a deliberate time delay in a batch processing workflow. It executes the program **COBSWAIT**, passing a value of **3600 centiseconds (36 seconds)** as input to control the wait duration. The job is typically used to pause job stream execution, allowing dependent processes, resources, or system conditions to reach a ready state before subsequent jobs proceed.

parameters.name: JOB NAME
parameters.description: The name assigned to the job, used to identify the job in the system and in job logs.

parameters.name: ACCOUNTING INFORMATION
parameters.description: Accounting information associated with the job, used for billing or tracking purposes.

parameters.name: CLASS
parameters.description: Specifies the job class, which determines the job entry subsystem (JES) queue where the job is placed for execution. Class A typically indicates a standard batch job class.

parameters.name: MSGCLASS
parameters.description: Specifies the output class for the job log and system messages. Class 0 determines where the job's message output (JCL listing, allocation/termination messages) is directed.

parameters.name: NOTIFY
parameters.description: Specifies the user ID to be notified when the job completes. The symbolic parameter &SYSUID resolves to the user ID of the person who submitted the job, so that user receives a notification upon job completion.

job_details.purpose: Executes the COBSWAIT program to introduce a timed delay of 36 seconds (3600 centiseconds) into the job stream. This is a wait utility used to pause job execution for a specified duration provided via SYSIN.
job_details.inputs: SYSIN (inline value: 00003600, representing 3600 centiseconds = 36 seconds wait duration)

data_operations.description: STEPLIB DD loads the COBSWAIT program from the customer application load library AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LOADLIB
SYSOUT DD directs program output messages to the system output class
SYSIN DD provides inline input data (value 00003600 in centiseconds, equating to 36 seconds) to the COBSWAIT program as its wait duration parameter
